normaliser: transformers EnglishTextNormalizer built from the openai/whisper-large-v3 normalizer.json spelling map (1740 entries): lowercase, punctuation removed, contractions expanded, British->American spelling, whitespace collapsed. Then, identically on both sides: any char not in [a-z0-9 ] becomes a space and each contiguous digit run is its own token (5.7 -> '5 7', 30% -> '30').
wer_formula: (S+D+I)/N, N = len(reference tokens), S/D/I from a Levenshtein backtrace with unit costs

passage_rule.rule: more matched keys wins; 0-0 is 'neither', a tie is 'ambiguous'

bootstrap.resample: speakers with replacement (one clip per speaker here, so speaker = clip)
bootstrap.paired: one speaker draw per replicate, both group means recomputed inside that draw

folds: not applicable: no cross-validated model is fitted in this task
prompt_text_condition: Based only on this transcript of what the person said, does this speaker show signs of Parkinson's disease? Answer with one word, Yes or No.
prompt_audio_condition: Based only on how this person's voice sounds, does this speaker show signs of Parkinson's disease? Answer with one word, Yes or No.

robustness.why: the per-clip mean cross-system disagreement is dominated by clips whose 30 s window caught almost no speech, so the WER denominator is tiny. ID11 has 10 reference words and 58 whisper-medium insertions, giving a single per-clip rate of 6.60 inside the control group.
robustness.reading: the sign of the group gap flips once the tiny-denominator clips stop dominating, and the paired interval straddles zero either way, so there is no reliable ASR-quality difference between the groups.

verification.method: independent recomputation from the per-clip csv: jiwer for the edit distance, a separate index-based bootstrap, AUC rewritten from the rank formula
verification.result: every point estimate, paired difference and Spearman interval agrees to 4 decimals; S, D and I agree exactly on all 37 clips for both alignments. Group-mean intervals differ in the last digits because the main script resamples within a group while the verifier draws all 37 speakers and subsets, e.g. B PD [0.1301, 0.4944] vs [0.1157, 0.5115].

answer.does_asr_quality_differ_by_group: no reliable difference. Every paired 2000-draw speaker interval straddles zero and the sign of the gap depends on how tiny-denominator clips are handled.
answer.does_asr_quality_track_the_transcript_de: partly. Whisper's own mean token logprob correlates with the transcript p_yes at Spearman -0.4009, p=0.0139, CI [-0.6720, -0.0835]: clips the ASR was less sure of get a higher Yes. But the same measure carries no diagnosis signal on its own (AUC 0.4792), so it cannot be what produces the 0.7634 transcript result.
answer.what_does_explain_it: reading material. The speakers were not given one common passage: north_wind PD=13/control=10, light_scattering PD=2/control=7, neither PD=1/control=4. Passage identity alone reaches AUC 0.6682 against the diagnosis, next to 0.7634 for the full transcript condition.
